routes.reason: Most craft advice is general drawing practice; the two compact drills directly activate perspective line/ellipse control and are worth retaining as transient drills.
The underlying perspective foundation is already present, but Robertson gives a useful exact viewing-position model, visual-ray VP derivation, and field-of-view framing.
Subdivision, mirroring, and curve transfer largely reinforce D’Amelio/White metrology; no duplicate cards are needed.
Same-scale grid rotation and Brewer off-page construction are genuine new tools; underlay and grid-model discussion materially sharpen the shared-scene/distortion system.
Ellipse control supports later rotations and volume work, but exact circle construction already exists and the broad axis theorem remains held for math verification.
This is Robertson’s major new capability: section-based complex-volume construction and controlled projection of cuts/curves onto those volumes.
Environment workflows mainly apply the mature scene-field system; wide-angle examples feed the distortion/math audit rather than a separate environment perspective card.
Aircraft and vehicle sections are rich applications of the new grid/section machinery, but subject design specialization is deferred to future domain passes.
Medium/style examples do not change perspective construction logic.

rationale: Robertson earns a selective Deep PASS rather than a whole-book Deep PASS: Chapters 4 and 6 add new construction machinery, Chapters 1-2/5 contribute targeted activation and exact-camera patches, and late subject/media chapters mainly validate portability and identify math-audit questions.
